The cover letter is not on any checklist. That is exactly why it works.

Most applications arrive as a pile of documents with nothing connecting them. The cover letter is where you answer what the form cannot: who you are, why this trip, why these dates, who is paying, and what you are returning to in the UAE.

It turns paper into a case.

We built a free generator that structures one around your profile.

slides.headline: THE DOCUMENT NOBODY TELLS YOU TO WRITE.
slides.sub: It is not on the checklist. That is the point.
slides.note: Without it, the officer receives documents with no story. With it, they receive a case.

slides.answer: THE FORM STATES FACTS. THE LETTER EXPLAINS THEM.
slides.body: Purpose, funding, and return — argued clearly, on one page, matched line for line to the documents enclosed.
slides.note: One page. Disproportionate effect on how the rest of the file reads.

slides.headline: WHAT A GOOD LETTER ANSWERS
items: Who you are and what you do in the UAE
Why this trip, and why these specific dates
Who is funding it, and where the proof sits
What you are returning to here
Anything unusual in your file, explained before it is questioned

slides.headline: WHY MOST LETTERS FAIL
slides.never: Download a template, change the name and the country, submit it. Consulates read hundreds of the same template every week. They can tell, and a generic letter adds nothing to your file.
slides.instead: Write it around your actual profile, your actual trip, and your actual documents — so every claim in it points at evidence you have enclosed.
